nodes.label: AudioClock class
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built Web Audio master-clock module (AudioContext.currentTime anchor) intended per README.md/project.md architecture docs to back HybridLipSyncController. Not referenced anywhere in public/lipsync-sdk.js, which reimplements an equivalent inline clock (_playPCM/_audioStart/_nextPlayAt) instead. todays_task.md task 4 explicitly flags this file as 'not confirmed wired up yet' and asks to verify usage or remove if dead; per prior session memory this was flagged and left as-is.

nodes.label: HybridLipSyncController class
nodes.rationale: Modular 3-mode (text/amplitude/neutral) lip-sync orchestrator composing AudioClock+VisemeMap+AmplitudeFallback+CharacterBehaviorController. The production embed widget (per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-04-lipsync-timing-and-emotions.md's Architecture note) loads only public/lipsync-sdk.min.js, which contains its own separate, duplicated implementation of this same pipeline — suggesting this file is currently unused in production despite being a complete, apparently-working alternative implementation.

nodes.label: AmplitudeFallback class
nodes.rationale: Standalone amplitude-driven jaw-motion fallback, designed to be composed by HybridLipSyncController. lipsync-sdk.js implements an equivalent inline FFT-band fallback (_runFFT + the amplitude branch of _driveSchedule) instead of importing this module — flagged in todays_task.md task 4 as a file whose wiring is unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Design rationale: byte-clock-windowed viseme timing
nodes.rationale: Gemini Live provides no phoneme-level timestamps, only audio chunks and transcript deltas, so viseme timing previously anchored each new delta to 'current audio position + a fixed 150ms guess', which drifts at chunk boundaries. Fix: use the audio scheduling clock the SDK already maintains (_nextPlayAt, accumulated from each chunk's exact byte-derived duration) as ground truth — measure how much real audio was scheduled since the previous transcript delta (windowMs) and scale the G2P-estimated phoneme durations to fit that real window, only when the window is plausible (80-4000ms), else fall back unchanged so the fix can only improve or preserve, never regress, timing.

nodes.label: Design rationale: multilingual, priority-ordered emotion reactions
nodes.rationale: Original reactToEmotion was English-only regex matching against the raw transcript delta, with negative-sentiment keywords not returning early — letting a thinking-look co-fire on top of a sad reaction — and a keyword split across two streaming chunks could be missed entirely. Fix: mutually-exclusive priority order (surprised > happy > sad > curious), per-language keyword tables keyed by detectLanguage()'s existing language codes (mirroring the G2P language-selection pattern), matching against the last ~60 chars of the accumulated transcript buffer instead of only the raw delta, plus an opts.emotionKeywords override hook mirroring the SDK's existing inputMap-style customization pattern.
nodes.norm_label: design rationale: multilingual, priority-ordered emotion reactions

nodes.label: Rejected: Gemini structured emotion tags & translation mode
nodes.rationale: Two alternative designs were explicitly ruled out during scoping: (1) a translation mode, and (2) driving expressions from Gemini-emitted structured emotion tags. The latter is not viable because the session uses response_modalities:['AUDIO'] — anything the model 'says' as a tag would be spoken aloud by the TTS voice rather than delivered as silent metadata, making keyword-regex-on-transcript the only workable signal.

nodes.label: Claude API Email-Parsing Fallback
nodes.rationale: Try a regex/HTML-structure parser first (fast, free, no API call); only fall back to the Claude API, prompted to return strict JSON (flight_datetime, duration_minutes, lesson_type, aircraft, instructor, status), when the regex parser cannot confidently extract a date/time. This mirrors the resume-parsing approach already used in RCIP Job Radar, reusing a proven pattern rather than inventing a new one.

nodes.label: Client-Owned Reminder Timing (design principle)
nodes.source_location: One-line summary; paragraph after Components table
nodes.rationale: Push delivery isn't guaranteed to arrive at the exact second, and a 2-hour alarm that's 4 minutes late because of network conditions defeats the point. Locally scheduled OS-level alarms (AlarmManager / UNNotificationRequest) are the reliable primitive, so the app -- not the backend -- owns all reminder timing; the backend's only job is making sure booking data is correct and current.

nodes.label: iOS Notification Service Extension (v2 fix)
nodes.source_location: Platform note: iOS is the hard part
nodes.rationale: iOS is much stricter about background execution and doesn't guarantee BGAppRefreshTask runs on a fixed schedule. v1 pragmatic fallback: skip conditional suppression, always fire the hourly reminder in the T-1h window (noisier but never silently misses) -- ship this first if iOS is needed immediately. v2 proper fix: a silent APNs push each interval triggers a Notification Service Extension, which can run a location check (with Always location permission) before the notification displays and can suppress or rewrite it, matching Android's behavior at the cost of more setup.

nodes.label: Fail-Open Failure Handling Principle
nodes.rationale: If the device can't get a GPS fix or has no connectivity at check time, fail open -- show the reminder rather than silently suppressing it. Missing a lesson is worse than one extra notification.

nodes.label: Airplane Flight Manual / Pilot's Operating Handbook (AFM/POH)
nodes.rationale: Originally each manufacturer used whatever flight-manual format it felt was appropriate. GAMA Specification No. 1 standardized the format across general aviation airplane and helicopter flight manuals into nine sections (General, Limitations, Emergency Procedures, Normal Procedures, Performance, Weight and Balance/Equipment List, Systems Description, Handling/Service/Maintenance, Supplements) so pilots can reliably find the operating limitations 14 CFR part 91 requires them to comply with, regardless of manufacturer.

nodes.label: Minimum Equipment List (MEL) / 91.213(d) deferral
nodes.source_location: p.9-9 to 9-10, MEL and Operations With Inoperative Equipment
nodes.rationale: The MEL concept lets aircraft fly with inoperative equipment judged nonessential for safe flight. The 14 CFR 91.213(d) deferral provision is popular because of its simplicity and minimal paperwork; once an operator requests an MEL and receives a Letter of Authorization, MEL use becomes mandatory for that aircraft and is treated by the FAA as equivalent to a supplemental type certificate for that specific serial-numbered aircraft.
